name: Ettumanoor Mahadeva Temple
tagline: A historic Shiva temple famed for murals and the Ezharapponnana (seven‑and‑a‑half golden elephants)
summary: Historic 16th‑century Shiva temple in Ettumanoor, Kottayam, known for its Pradosha Nritham mural, Travancore connections and the annual Ezharapponnana festival.
description: Ettumanoor Mahadeva Temple is an important Shiva shrine in Ettumanoor town, Kottayam district. The present complex and the famous wall paintings date from the medieval/early modern period and the temple figures among Kerala’s notable heritage temples.

The temple is best known for its rich mural program — including the celebrated Pradosha Nritham — and for the Ezharapponnana (the seven‑and‑a‑half golden elephant figures) that draw large crowds during the annual festival in Kumbham (Malayalam month falling around February–March).

The shrine also has historic links with the Travancore royals and the Travancore Devaswom Board manages routine upkeep and festival arrangements. Visitors come for religious darshan, to see the murals and for the colourful festival rituals and processions.

Practical visitor details such as daily darshan hours, special entry rules during festivals and donation/pooja charges change from time to time — confirm before you travel with the temple office or official sources.
highlights: Pradosha Nritham — one of the temple’s best‑known mural panels
Ezharapponnana — the seven‑and‑a‑half gold‑clad elephant figures displayed during the annual festival
Centuries‑old murals across the gopuram inner and outer walls
Travancore royal associations and traditional Kerala temple architecture
Major festival (Thiru Ulsavam) in Kumbham with processions, pallivetta and aarattu

sections.heading: Background
body: The temple has a long recorded history and is widely described as an important Mahadeva (Shiva) shrine in central Kerala; many sources date the existing complex and its fame to the early modern period (often cited as 16th century in tourism literature).

Local tradition links the temple to the Travancore rulers — the royal family is credited with presenting the Ezharapponnana and with historic patronage that shaped the temple’s ritual culture. The Travancore Devaswom Board currently administers the temple.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Study the mural cycles on the gopuram and inner walls — notable panels include Pradosha Nritham, Ananthasayanam, Kaliyamardhanam and Vetta scenes. These murals underwent a conservation project that returned many panels to public view.

If you visit during the annual festival (Kumbham, usually Feb–Mar) you can witness Ezharapponnana darshan (the display of seven‑and‑a‑half golden elephants), Pallivetta and the Aarattu procession. Outside festival days the temple offers quieter darshan and an opportunity to appreciate traditional Kerala temple architecture.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Location and access: Ettumanoor town lies north of Kottayam. Nearest railway: Ettumanoor station (about 2 km); Kottayam town is about 10–12 km away. Cochin International Airport is the closest major airport (roughly 70–80 km depending on route). Confirm travel connections locally before you go.

Practicalities: The temple has large crowds during Ezharapponnana and festival days; expect traffic management and security measures in place. Do not assume fixed visiting hours or photography rules — check with temple notice boards or the official temple contact before travelling. Respect dress and behaviour norms typical at Kerala temples.

latest.text: A year‑long conservation project of the temple’s centuries‑old murals concluded and the restored paintings were formally dedicated; restoration work covered several major panels including Pradosha Nritham.

Travancore Devaswom Board published tenders (re‑tenders) in January 2026 for maintenance works related to the Ettumanoor group, including parking/tarring and structural maintenance ahead of festival season.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Kumbham (Feb–Mar) for festival events like Ezharapponnana; November–February for cooler, drier weather and easier sightseeing.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Ettumanoor is on the Kottayam–Thodupuzha corridor. Nearest rail: Ettumanoor station (~2 km). Kottayam town is ~10–12 km. Cochin International Airport is roughly 70–80 km by road. Local buses, taxis and autorickshaws serve the temple area.
etiquette: Dress modestly and follow temple etiquette; confirm any photography rules at the entrance.
Festival days attract large crowds and traffic controls; arrive early and follow police/temple signage.
Confirm darshan hours and special entry procedures (especially for Ezharapponnana) with the temple office before you travel.
If you want to study the murals closely, contact the temple or local heritage groups to learn about viewing opportunities and conservation restrictions.
